data.name: Khiyar
data.gender_notes: Khiyar is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'Kh-Y-R', meaning 'to be free from' or 'to be exempt from'. In Islamic context, it is used to describe God's mercy and forgiveness. The name Khiyar carries the meaning “Free, Exempt” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Khiyar usually hope their child will grow to embody free, exempt and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of God's mercy and forgiveness.
data.etymology: Khiyar belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Free, Exempt.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Khiyar total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_arabic.name: خيار
in_arabic.meaning: خيار تعني اختيار أو انتقاء الشيء الأفضل
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم خيار مشتق من الفعل اختار، وهو يعني اختيار الشيء الأفضل أو الانتقاء بحكمة. ورد في القرآن الكريم في عدة مواضع، منها قول الله تعالى: ﴿فَخَرِصَ مِنكُم مّن يَكُفُرُ وَمَن يَأْمَنُ عَلَى الرَّسُولِ وَأُولِي الْأَمْرِ مِنكُمْ وَمَن يَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ﴾ [النساء: 59]. يدل الاسم على معنى الإختيار والتمييز بين الخير والشر.

in_urdu.name: خیار
in_urdu.meaning: خیار کا مطلب ہے انتخاب کرنا یا بہترین چیز کا انتخاب کرنا
in_urdu.long_meaning: نام خیار عربی زبان کے فعل 'اختار' سے ماخوذ ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے کسی چیز کا انتخاب کرنا یا بہترین چیز کا انتخاب کرنا۔ اسلامی تقالید میں اس نام کا استعمال اہم ہے کیونکہ یہ اللہ تعالی کی قدرت و حکمت کو ظاہر کرتا ہے جو اپنے بندوں کو بہترین کا انتخاب کرنے کی ہدایت کرتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: ख़ियार
in_hindi.meaning: ख़ियार का अर्थ है चयन करना या सर्वोत्तम चीज़ का चयन करना
in_hindi.long_meaning: नाम ख़ियार अरबी भाषा के क्रिया 'इख़्तियार' से लिया गया है, जिसका अर्थ है किसी चीज़ का चयन करना या सर्वोत्तम चीज़ का चयन करना। भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में इस नाम का उपयोग महत्वपूर्ण है क्योंकि यह अल्लाह की शक्ति और ज्ञान को दर्शाता है जो अपने अनुयायियों को श्रेष्ठ का चयन करने के लिए प्रेरित करता है।

in_pashto.name: خیار
in_pashto.meaning: خیار د انتخاب یا د غوره شیانو د ټاکلو معنی لري
in_pashto.long_meaning: د خیار نوم د عربي ژبې د 'اختار' فعل څخه اخیستل شوی دی، چې معنی یې د انتخاب یا د غوره شیانو د ټاکلو څخه ده. په افغان او پښتون قومونو کې ددې نوم کارول مهم دی ځکه چې دا د الله تعالی قدرت او حکمت ښیي چې خپلو بنده ګانو ته د غوره انتخاب لپاره لارښوونه کوي.

in_english.name: Khiyar
in_english.meaning: Khiyar means to choose or select the best thing
in_english.long_meaning: The name Khiyar is derived from the Arabic verb 'khtr', which means to choose or select. It appears in several contexts in the Quran, emphasizing the concept of choosing the best or making a wise decision. The name signifies wisdom, discernment, and the ability to distinguish between good and evil, reflecting a positive and guiding attribute in Islamic tradition.

data.cultural_impact: In Islamic culture, the name "Khiyar" holds significance in various aspects of life. For instance, in property law, a Khiyar (sometimes also called Iqrah) is a form of sale contract where the buyer has the right to cancel the transaction within a specific period before delivers the goods. This name is used across the Muslim world, reflects the importance of justice and fairness in business transactions.
data.spiritual_significance: "Khiyar" holds deep spiritual significance in Islam, representing the mercy and forgiveness of Allah (God). It is mentioned in various Hadiths and Quranic verses. For example, in Surah Ar-Ra'd (35:3), Allah says, "It is He Who gives you the news of the occasion both (news) of happiness and (news) for despair that you had not known. But out of His knowledge, He is Forgiving, Most Merciful." The name, thus, invokes the profound feeling of gratitude and reliance on Allah's mercy.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun records the sale of lands called Khiyar in his book 'The Muqaddimah'. This sale was a common practice in the Maghreb during the Marinid and Hafsid eras (13th-15th centuries). The land was sold with the condition that it could be redeemed by its original owner after a specified period of time.

Al-Maqrizi, an Egyptian historian, mentions the Khiyar system of selling agricultural lands in his book 'The History of the Prophets and the Kings'. This practice was prevalent in Egypt during the Mamluk Sultanate (13th-16th centuries). Farmers could sell their lands and rent them back from the new owners and regain possession after a set period of time.
